To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(a) there is a low degree of inter-link consistency and (b) there is a weak relationship between levels of inter-link consistency in hypertext databases and retrieval effectiveness.

(i) there is little similarity amongst link-sets created by different link-assigners, and (ii) no relationship exists between the levels of inter-index consistency and those of retrieval effectiveness.

(i) there is little inter-linker consistency in hypertext databases; (ii) there is no evidence that the level of inter-linker similarity is related to the level of effectiveness of the searches that are carried out; and (iii) the effectiveness of the searches is related to the size of the database.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of whether or not it is necessary to achieve a high level of agreement amongst link-sets in order to achieve a high retrieval effectiveness.
the question of how well the links assigned by a human indexer can be used in the process of information retrieval, and with the question of what factors may affect the effectiveness of such links.

the development and testing of a model that can be used in the evaluation of the effectiveness of retrieval systems that are based upon the use of inter-object links, and that may also have application to the evaluation of conventional retrieval systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is no evidence to suggest that there is a positive relationship between inter-linker consistency in a hypertext database and its retrieval effectiveness.
the relationship is weak, but that it is nevertheless positive, and that it is not significantly affected by the nature of the database or by the number of links in it.
there is no significant relationship between the two variables.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the results obtained suggest that the level of inter-linker agreement is not an effective indicator of the retrieval effectiveness that may ultimately be obtained in a given hypertext database.

there is little evidence of the existence of a positive relationship between inter-linker consistency levels and retrieval effectiveness, although the possibility remains that the lack of a relationship may have been due to the fact that the link-sets were created by only a few people.

, whilst it is possible to achieve some measure of agreement between different linkers, the levels of inter-indexing consistency that may be obtained are not necessarily reflected in the retrieval effectiveness that may subsequently be achieved. The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the context of hypertext databases, the relationship is not positive, but is in fact negative.

there is no positive correlation between inter-linker consistency levels and retrieval effectiveness, and that the latter is best improved by the introduction of additional links, rather than by the refinement of those already in place.

, as in conventional retrieval systems, there exists no positive correlation between the level of inter-linker agreement and the effectiveness with which objects may be retrieved from a hypertext system.
